answer: Sybil resistance rests on a depositor-funded bond slashed per verified collusion. An operator escrows a stake above expected gain from one epoch, and payouts vest only after a challenge round. A thousand synthetic keys need a thousand escrows, so attacker cost scales with identity count while rewards dilute, making the marginal fake key unprofitable before capture. A proven cluster forfeits the whole glacier behind it, and shared-address linkage spreads that penalty to the cohort, leaving a karst only implausible capital can fill. A velvet of honest return keeps entry cheap.
